instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Open the Homebrew Formulae page for ffmpeg
criteria.description: Use the Homebrew Formulae website (formulae.brew.sh) to access the ffmpeg formula details page. Full credit if the agent reaches the page OR clearly reports an uncontrollable blocker (site down, access blocked/CAPTCHA, network error) preventing access after a reasonable attempt. Partial credit if the agent uses an alternative source without first attempting the specified page.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows State 1 at https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg and a scroll action. Screenshot 1 shows the Homebrew Formulae page titled “ffmpeg” with install command and site branding; Screenshot 2 shows the same formula page sections (Current versions, bottle/platform table). Latest is Screenshot 2 and it is consistent with being on the ffmpeg formula page.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The page was successfully opened and is clearly the Homebrew Formulae ffmpeg formula page. No blocker is shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Homebrew Formulae site with the header text “Homebrew Formulae” and the formula page title “ffmpeg”. It includes an “Install command:” line showing “$ brew install ffmpeg”, and “Also known as: ffmpeg@9”. The page layout and URL are not visible in the screenshot, but the branding and formula content indicate the ffmpeg formula page on formulae.brew.sh.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Meets the criterion. The screenshot clearly shows the Homebrew Formulae ffmpeg formula details page (title “ffmpeg” and install command). No blocker is visible.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy for reaching the page; the screenshot supports that ffmpeg’s formula page is open.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows part of a Homebrew Formulae-style page section with bottle/platform rows labeled “macOS on Apple Silicon”, “macOS on Intel”, and “Linux”. Under “macOS on Apple Silicon”, the entries “Tahoe”, “Sequoia”, and “Sonoma” are visible. Under “Linux”, “ARM64” and “x86_64” are visible. A “Current versions:” block is visible and an “Other versions:” list containing “ffmpeg@8”, “ffmpeg@7”, etc. is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This is consistent with being on the ffmpeg formula page on formulae.brew.sh (it shows ffmpeg-related version blocks and bottle/platform availability UI). The screenshot provides reasonable evidence the agent reached the ffmpeg formula details page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No clear discrepancy for page access; however the screenshot does not show the browser URL bar, so the exact URL cannot be directly verified from pixels.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 and state 1 both show URL https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg with title 'Homebrew Formulae: ffmpeg' and visible formula name 'ffmpeg'. Latest is state 1; it still confirms the ffmpeg formula page is open.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Baseline already gave full credit and DOM evidence supports that the agent reached the correct Homebrew Formulae ffmpeg page with no blocker.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL "https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg" and Title "Homebrew Formulae: ffmpeg".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM snapshot confirms the required Homebrew Formulae page for the ffmpeg formula is open at formulae.brew.sh.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy between required page and observed URL/title in the DOM snapshot.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL "https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/ffmpeg" and Title "Homebrew Formulae: ffmpeg" with visible content including "Homebrew Formulae" and the formula name "ffmpeg".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM snapshot explicitly indicates the Homebrew Formulae site is open on the ffmpeg formula page at the required formulae.brew.sh URL.

criteria.description: Report the stable version exactly as shown on the ffmpeg formula page once accessible. Full credit for an exact match to the page’s stable version label/value. Partial credit if a version is reported but is from a different section (e.g., HEAD) or not clearly identified as stable. If the page is accessible but the stable version is not visible due to page rendering/section not loading, award full credit if the agent explicitly states that it is not displayed/accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest relevant) shows “Current versions:” with the row labeled “stable” displaying version “9.0.1”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent output reports stable version 9.0.1, which matches the stable version shown in Screenshot 2.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the “Current versions:” section, the row labeled “stable” shows version “9.0.1”. The “head” row shows “HEAD”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot directly supports the agent’s reported stable version of 9.0.1; it matches exactly what is displayed next to “stable”.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None for the stable version value; it matches the visible “stable 9.0.1”.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) explicitly shows 'Current versions: stable ✅ 9.0.1'.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Although baseline was 0 due to lack of action-history extraction, the DOM evidence confirms the stable version is 9.0.1 and the agent reported 9.0.1 correctly. Full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 VISIBLE CONTENT includes: "Current versions: stable ✅ 9.0.1 head ⚡️ HEAD".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The stable version is explicitly shown as 9.0.1 in the DOM.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the reported stable version (9.0.1) matches the DOM text for the stable version.

criteria.description: Report the license value exactly as displayed on the ffmpeg formula page once accessible. Full credit for an exact license string. Partial credit if the license is approximate/incomplete. If the page is accessible but the license is not visible due to page rendering/section not loading, award full credit if the agent explicitly states that it is not displayed/accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest relevant for license) shows “License: GPL-3.0-or-later”. Screenshot 2 does not display license.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent output reports license GPL-3.0-or-later, which matches Screenshot 1 exactly.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: A line on the page reads “License: GPL-3.0-or-later”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Meets the criterion. The agent’s predicted output lists the license as “GPL-3.0-or-later,” which matches exactly what is visible.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows 'License: GPL-3.0-or-later' (also present in state 0).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: DOM evidence supports the agent’s reported license exactly as displayed. Update from baseline 0 to full credit.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The license is explicitly shown as GPL-3.0-or-later in the DOM.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the reported license (GPL-3.0-or-later) matches the DOM text.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 visible content includes "License: GPL-3.0-or-later" and also shows "GPL-3.0-or-later" on its own line.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The license value is directly shown in the DOM as "GPL-3.0-or-later".

criteria.criterion: Record complete regular dependency list (Depends on)
criteria.description: List every package shown under the regular 'Depends on' section for ffmpeg, excluding build-only dependencies and excluding items under 'Uses from macOS'. Full credit if all and only the regular 'Depends on' packages are captured as displayed. Partial credit if some regular dependencies are missing or extra items are included (e.g., build-only deps or 'Uses from macOS'). If the page is accessible but the 'Depends on' section is not visible/does not load, award full credit if the agent clearly reports that the section is not displayed/accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Neither Screenshot 1 nor Screenshot 2 displays the “Depends on” section at all; therefore there is no visual evidence supporting the specific dependency list the agent provided.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Because the regular “Depends on” list is not visible in the provided screenshots, the agent’s dependency list cannot be verified from evidence and appears unsupported (potential fabrication). No uncontrollable blocker is evidenced; the agent likely needed to scroll further to capture the section but did not.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the top section of the ffmpeg formula page (install command, alias, description, website link, license, development link, JSON API link, and formula code link). It does not show any “Depends on” section or any dependency list. Near the bottom, it begins to show “Bottle (binary package) installation support provided for:” but the actual bottle table and any dependencies are not visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Not supported by the screenshot. Because the “Depends on” section is not visible, the screenshot cannot verify the agent’s listed dependencies. The agent did not state that the section was inaccessible; instead they provided a full dependency list, which is not corroborated by this image.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output includes a complete regular dependency list (dav1d, lame, libvmaf, etc.), but the screenshot contains no visible dependency section to confirm any of those items.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows “Current versions:” and “Other versions:” (listing ffmpeg@8 8.1.2, ffmpeg@7 7.1.5, ffmpeg@6 6.1.6, ffmpeg@5 5.1.10, ffmpeg@4 4.4.8, ffmpeg@2.8 2.8.22). There is no visible “Depends on” section or any dependency list in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output lists a set of regular dependencies, but the screenshot provides no evidence for any of those packages because the “Depends on” section is not visible. Therefore, from this screenshot alone, completeness/correctness of the dependency list cannot be confirmed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims an 11-item “Depends on” list (dav1d, lame, libvmaf, etc.), but none of these are shown anywhere in the screenshot; this portion of the output is unsupported by the provided visual evidence.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows 'Depends on:' with 11 packages: dav1d, lame, libvmaf, libvpx, openssl@3, opus, sdl2-compat, svt-av1, x264, x265, xz. It separately shows 'Depends on when building from source: pkgconf' and 'Uses from macOS: bzip2, libxml2' (to be excluded per task).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent listed exactly the 11 regular dependencies and correctly excluded build-only and 'Uses from macOS' items. Update from baseline 0 to full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows the heading "Depends on:" and Table 2 lists 11 packages: "dav1d", "lame", "libvmaf", "libvpx", "openssl@3", "opus", "sdl2-compat", "svt-av1", "x264", "x265", "xz". It also separately shows "Depends on when building from source:" and Table 3 lists "pkgconf"; and shows "Uses from macOS: bzip2 , libxml2".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The complete regular "Depends on" list is present and can be read directly from the DOM (Table 2). Excluding build-only deps ("Depends on when building from source:" -> pkgconf) and excluding "Uses from macOS" (bzip2, libxml2), the regular dependencies are exactly the 11 packages in Table 2.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the agent’s dependency list matches the 11 packages shown in the regular "Depends on" table, and correctly excludes build-only (pkgconf) and "Uses from macOS" (bzip2, libxml2).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 visible content does not include any "Depends on" section or dependency names; it only shows general header info (install command, also known as, description, homepage link, license, and bottle support header).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
The provided DOM snapshot does not contain the regular "Depends on" section, so it cannot support (or contradict) the agent’s claimed dependency list.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output lists dependencies (dav1d, lame, libvmaf, libvpx, openssl@3, opus, sdl2-compat, svt-av1, x264, x265, xz), but none of these appear in the available DOM evidence; completeness/accuracy cannot be verified from this state.

criteria.criterion: Record bottle availability for macOS Apple Silicon and for Linux
criteria.description: Report whether binary bottles are displayed/available exactly as shown on the ffmpeg formula page for (1) macOS on Apple Silicon and (2) Linux. Full credit if both platforms are addressed and wording matches the page display (including any labels/table text). Partial credit if only one platform is reported or the wording is not as displayed. If the page is accessible but bottle information is not displayed (no bottle table/section shown or it fails to load), award full credit if the agent explicitly states that bottle availability is not displayed/accessible for the requested platforms.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest relevant) shows the bottle/platform table with sections “macOS on Apple Silicon” listing “Tahoe”, “Sequoia”, “Sonoma” (each with bottle indicators) and “Linux” listing “ARM64” and “x86_64” (each with indicators).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent output reports bottle availability for macOS on Apple Silicon as Tahoe/Sequoia/Sonoma and for Linux as ARM64/x86_64, matching the platform labels displayed. Minor formatting difference (agent used checkmarks) but the requested availability as displayed is captured.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the bottle/platform area, under “macOS on Apple Silicon” the entries “Tahoe”, “Sequoia”, and “Sonoma” are visible, each with a small bottle/icon indicator to the right. Under “Linux”, “ARM64” and “x86_64” are visible, each also with an indicator icon to the right.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that bottles are displayed for macOS on Apple Silicon for Tahoe/Sequoia/Sonoma and for Linux for ARM64/x86_64. This aligns with the agent’s statement that these platforms show bottle availability (agent used checkmarks; screenshot shows the presence of the bottle/icon indicators).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Minor formatting mismatch: the agent reports availability with “✅” symbols; the screenshot shows small bottle-style icons/indicators rather than explicit checkmarks. The listed platform/version labels themselves (Tahoe, Sequoia, Sonoma; ARM64, x86_64) match what is visible.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows bottle support: 'macOS on Apple Silicon' with tahoe ✅, sequoia ✅, sonoma ✅; and 'Linux' with ARM64 ✅ and x86_64 ✅.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent’s bottle availability matches the latest DOM exactly for both requested platforms. Update from baseline 0 to full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 VISIBLE CONTENT includes: "Bottle (binary package) installation support provided for: macOS on Apple Silicon tahoe ✅ sequoia ✅ sonoma ✅ ... Linux ARM64 ✅ x86_64 ✅".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
Bottle availability for the requested platforms is explicitly displayed in the DOM: macOS on Apple Silicon has bottles for tahoe, sequoia, sonoma (all ✅), and Linux has ARM64 and x86_64 (both ✅).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the agent’s bottle availability report matches the DOM text for macOS on Apple Silicon (tahoe ✅, sequoia ✅, sonoma ✅) and Linux (ARM64 ✅, x86_64 ✅).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 includes a bottle table (Table 1) labeled under "Bottle (binary package) installation support provided for:" with rows for "macOS on Apple Silicon | tahoe | ✅" and subsequent rows "sequoia | ✅" and "sonoma | ✅". No Linux bottle rows/table are present in this DOM snapshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM explicitly shows bottle availability for macOS on Apple Silicon (tahoe ✅, sequoia ✅, sonoma ✅), but does not show any bottle availability information for Linux in the provided snapshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output additionally claims Linux bottles "ARM64 ✅" and "x86_64 ✅"; Linux evidence is not present in the DOM snapshot, so that portion is unverified.

criteria.description: Do not download or install the formula; use only the regular 'Depends on' section (excluding build-only and 'Uses from macOS'); and stop after recording stable version, license, the complete regular dependency list, and bottle availability for macOS Apple Silicon and Linux. Full credit if all constraints are followed. Partial credit if minor extra unrelated info is included but the requested items are still correct and constraints are not violated. No credit if major constraints are violated (e.g., includes build-only/Uses from macOS as dependencies, or claims to have installed/downloaded).

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots show only browsing/scrolling on the formula page, with no installs/downloads. However, screenshots do not show the Depends on section, so it is not verifiable that the agent used the regular Depends on section or excluded build-only/Uses from macOS items. The agent stopped after reporting the requested fields.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Constraints about not downloading/installing appear satisfied, and the agent did stop after providing the requested categories. But because the dependency list is unsupported and the page evidence does not show the Depends on section, the key constraint ‘use the regular Depends on section’ is not met in a verifiable way (and is likely violated via unsupported reporting). Deduct for that major constraint failure while retaining credit for no-install and stopping condition behavior.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Visible content includes “Install command: $ brew install ffmpeg” and “License: GPL-3.0-or-later”. The screenshot does not show stable version, does not show the “Depends on” section, and only partially shows the heading “Bottle (binary package) installation support provided for:” without the platform rows (macOS Apple Silicon / Linux) being visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partially meets constraints but overall not verifiable/complete from the screenshot. There is no evidence of downloading/installing. However, the stopping-condition items (stable version, full regular Depends on list, and bottle availability for Apple Silicon macOS and Linux) are not visible here, so the agent’s completion claims can’t be confirmed from this screenshot. Also, the predicted output includes bottle availability details (e.g., Tahoe/Sequoia/Sonoma; Linux ARM64/x86_64) that are not displayed in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Predicted output claims stable version “9.0.1” and specific bottle availability for macOS Apple Silicon and Linux, but the screenshot shows neither the stable version field nor the bottle entries for those platforms—only the bottle section header is partially visible.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot contains no evidence of downloading or installing. It shows version/bottle UI and a list of other ffmpeg formula versions. It does not show the license field or any “Depends on” section.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: No sign of violating the ‘do not download/install’ constraint is visible. However, the agent’s output includes a license and a full dependency list, neither of which are visible in this screenshot; additionally, the instruction required using the regular “Depends on” section—since it isn’t shown here, compliance with that specific sourcing can’t be verified from the image. The agent also did stop after the requested items in their response format, but two of those items (license, dependencies) are not evidenced by the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent provides “License: GPL-3.0-or-later” and a full dependency list, but neither appears in the screenshot; thus those claims are not supported by the visible page portion. No discrepancy regarding downloading/installing (none shown).

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 shows only viewing the formula page (includes an install command string but no execution). It also shows distinct sections for regular 'Depends on', build-only dependencies, and 'Uses from macOS', enabling validation that the agent used the correct dependency section.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: No evidence of downloading/installing; the dependency list used is the regular 'Depends on' list per constraints; output stops after requested items. Baseline full credit remains appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows only browsing of the formula page and an install command string ("brew install ffmpeg") but no evidence of executing installs. It also shows separate sections: "Depends on:", "Depends on when building from source:", and "Uses from macOS" which allows checking that only the regular "Depends on" list was used.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
Constraints appear respected based on the provided output and DOM: no downloading/installing is evidenced; the dependency list corresponds to the regular "Depends on" section and excludes build-only and "Uses from macOS" items; and the agent stopped after providing stable version, license, dependencies, and bottle availability for the requested platforms.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: nothing indicates the formula was installed/downloaded, and no extra dependency sections were improperly included in the regular dependency list.
